reframing_when: The question operates within a theoretical framework so deeply accepted that anomalies and contradictions are explained away rather than taken as evidence that the frame itself might be wrong.
The question treats an established model or theory as ground truth rather than as one possible lens — the theory has become invisible infrastructure rather than a testable assumption.
The question dismisses evidence that contradicts the dominant framework as noise, exceptions, or measurement error rather than asking whether the framework itself is the source of distortion.
The question frames refinement of the existing theory as the only path forward when the anomalies actually point toward a fundamentally different explanatory frame.
reframing_move: Before refining the current theory, ask: 'What anomalies am I explaining away, and what alternative framework would treat those anomalies as the central evidence?' — the theory-blindness reframe makes the dominant theory visible as a choice rather than as reality.
curation_note: Theory-Induced Blindness is a primary reframing model — Kahneman coined the term to describe how accepted theories make their own flaws invisible. The source describes how 'once you have accepted a theory and used it as a tool in your thinking, it is extraordinarily difficult to notice its flaws' and how anomalies are 'absorbed' rather than challenged. The borrowed_premise challenge is direct: the theory is a borrowed frame. The habitual_frame challenge maps to the model's description of theories becoming invisible cognitive infrastructure.

reframing_when.note: Anomaly absorption (source's core mechanism), invisible infrastructure (theory as 'tool in your thinking'), evidence dismissal ('extraordinarily difficult to notice flaws'), refinement trap (the model's description of incremental patching vs paradigm shift).

frame_patterns_challenged.note: Borrowed premise: accepted theory functions as imported frame. Habitual frame: theory becomes invisible default. Counterfactual suppression: anomalies that point to alternatives are absorbed. Scope lock: theory constrains what counts as relevant evidence.
